Speedup = 1.0: baseline FID saturates at NFE=10 (66.73, Euler); framework also saturates at NFE=10 (66.65). Both reach 95% at same NFE on this Euler grid. Extends-plateau evidence: framework at NFE=2 (FID 122.18) beats baseline at NFE=2 (FID 218.87) by 44.17%, but at matched NFE=50 framework is WORSE (103.41 vs 83.09). speedup_summary.note: All directly-measured Tier 1 speedups are 1.0. The 2D FM 5-10x speedup is extrapolated, not measured (nfe_95_baseline is unknown because only 1 baseline NFE point exists). CIFAR-10 RF saturates at NFE=10 for both baseline and framework on this Euler grid (1st-order).

extends_plateau_models: cifar10_rf (at NFE=2 only; NOT at NFE=10/50)

framework_vs_2026_sota.vs_dpm_solver: DPM-Solver (Lu 2022, NeurIPS Oral) achieves CIFAR-10 FID 4.70 at NFE=10 (4x-16x vs previous samplers) via exploiting semi-linear ODE structure. Framework's CIFAR-10 reaches parity at NFE=10 (FID 66.65) but does not reach DPM-Solver's headline (which requires Heun 2nd-order + careful tuning). Framework's CIFAR-10 value-add is at very low NFE (NFE=2): framework 122.18 vs baseline 218.87 (-44.17%).
framework_vs_2026_sota.vs_consistency_model: Consistency Models (Song 2023, ICML, ~2000 citations) achieves CIFAR-10 FID 3.55 in 1 step via retraining (consistency distillation). Speedup ~1000x vs DDPM but requires model retraining. Framework is training-free and stacks on top of any solver; cannot match Consistency Models' 1-step result on CIFAR-10 without retraining.
framework_vs_2026_sota.vs_rectified_flow: Rectified Flow (Liu 2022, ICLR) uses straight-line ODEs for fast generation. Published 1-RF reaches FID 2.58 on CIFAR-10 (50K samples, Heun adaptive, NFE=100+). Framework's Rectified Flow adapter (1st-order Euler, 500 samples, NFE<=50) reaches FID 83.09 baseline / 103.41 framework at matched NFE=50 — 32x worse than published due to sample count (100x fewer) + solver order (1st vs 2nd order).

honest_caveats: The 2D FM (Two Moons + Eight Gaussians) 5-10x speedup is EXTRAPOLATED from published Liu 2022 Rectified Flow SOTA, NOT directly measured. Existing R4 data has only ONE baseline NFE point (NFE=500); cannot compute NFE_95 from a single-point baseline curve. Phase 2 P2-1 baseline NFE-scan at NFE in {500, 1000, 2000, 5000} is required to directly measure Tier 1 2D FM speedup.

The CIFAR-10 RF speedup is 1.0 on this Euler grid: both baseline (FID 66.73) and framework (FID 66.65) saturate at NFE=10. Published Liu 2022 FID 2.58 requires Heun adaptive solver + NFE=100+ + 50K samples (32x gap from this Euler grid).

MNIST FM framework reaches parity within G.3 noise (signed_mean +0.0625). The DPM++ baseline collapses l2_norm to 2.84 at NFE=20 via proxy collapse; framework value-add on MNIST is composite, not NFE-budget reduction.

Cross-check vs Wave 71 Phase 5 Tier 3: Tier 3 (Kanzi + LineageFlow + FlowMol3) also reports speedup_95 = 1.0 (all metrics saturate at smallest NFE). However the Tier 1 + Tier 3 conclusions are STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT: Tier 3 metrics are designed to saturate at NFE=10 by metric property (validity rate), so 1.0 is correct. Tier 1 metrics (W2 / FID) do NOT saturate at NFE=10 by metric property — the 1.0 is because the available NFE-scan data is insufficient (R4 has only 1 baseline NFE point per model).

Extends-baseline-plateau evidence is STRONG for 2D FM at matched NFE=500: framework W2 is below baseline saturation W2 by 7.28% (Two Moons) and 10.40% (Eight Gaussians). For CIFAR-10 RF extends-plateau is TRUE at NFE=2 (framework -44.17% vs baseline) but FALSE at matched NFE=10 (parity) and matched NFE=50 (framework 24.46% WORSE). The framework's CIFAR-10 RF 'extends-plateau' claim requires the framework to be run at HIGH NFE per round (e.g., NFE=200 per round × 10 rounds = 2000 NFE total) to extend beyond the baseline's NFE=100+ plateau — not yet run.

The 2D FM extends-plateau evidence is the strongest Tier 1 result: framework W2 at NFE=500 (matched to baseline NFE=500) is below baseline W2 at NFE=500. This is direct evidence that the framework reaches a qualitatively different endpoint (W2 closer to the analytic two-moons / eight-gaussians target) without spending more NFE.
Constraint compliance: READ-ONLY (no code changes), no commit, no push. All numbers come from existing verification_outputs/*.json + docs/r4-survey/*.md files; no new measurements were performed.
notes: Tier 1 Wave 17 noise-injection baseline (W2 ~0.11) uses a different trained velocity field than the R4 baseline (W2 = 0.5029). The two cannot be directly compared. The Wave 17 framework W2 (0.3270) is also a different velocity field from R4 framework W2 (0.4663). The cleanest Tier 1 NFE-vs-quality data is internally consistent: (R4 baseline @ NFE=500 → W2=0.5029) and (R4 framework @ 10 rounds × cosine ramp → W2=0.4663) — both on the same trained velocity field.

Wave R4 baseline NFE=500 is a 1-pass single-round solve. Wave R4 framework runs 10-20 rounds × cosine ramp of num_steps (1.0 → 0.0) so total framework NFE budget = 10 × avg(500 * cosine) ≈ 2500. The framework's W2 reduction (-7.28% / -10.40%) is achieved at HIGHER total NFE budget (2500 vs 500). The 'speedup' claim therefore requires the baseline to need MORE NFE to reach the framework's W2 — this is exactly what the Phase 2 P2-1 baseline NFE-scan is supposed to measure.

Wave 71 Phase 5 cross-model verdict ('Tier 3 speedup = 1.0') is structurally different from this Tier 1 verdict: Tier 3 metrics are designed to saturate at NFE=10 by metric property (validity_rate = 1.0 is the ceiling; framework lifts a different metric called 'composite'); Tier 1 metrics (W2, FID) have no such ceiling but the existing NFE-scan data is insufficient to measure Tier 1 speedup directly.

Cross-tier consistency verdict: BOTH Tier 1 and Tier 3 report speedup_ratio = 1.0, but for DIFFERENT reasons. The paper framing should be: 'Tier 1 has convergence-speedup that is extrapolated but not directly measured (5-10x from Liu 2022 published trajectory); Tier 3 has constant composite lift (NFE-independent, measured directly).'

Phase 2 P2-1 + P2-2 baseline NFE-scan (CPU, ~30 min) would close the Tier 1 speedup question directly. P2-4 + P2-5 + P2-6 (GPU, ~4-5 hours) would extend the CIFAR-10 RF NFE grid from {2, 10, 50} to {2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 20, 50, 100} with Heun solver.
